newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil ends neutral, barges up on bunker need.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil ends neutral, barges up on bunker need.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets finished the week on a neutral note, with barges supported by bunker demand and low sulphur cracked tight in the very prompt period, traders said.
Barges bounced back, with traders pegging $81 fob as the current market floor, with high prices in Singapore lending mild encouragement to bunker demand in Europe, players said.
Physical deals were done in the range from $82 to $83.75 fob ARA. "It was mainly boosted by local demand and short-covering from yesterday, though overall the market was thin," said one barge trader.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes got a little boost from reports that a U.S. refiner/traders was looking for top-up material, which would dry up prompt supplies.
Further out the low sulphur grade looked well supplied.

High sulphur cargo markets were static with participants watching reports that cracked material may flow from the Mediterranean to the Far East. Opinion differed on the strength of support this would offer to the northern market.
